title: Manual tri-star hand truck v4 for one courier with 60 kg parcel
problem_restatement: Provide a one-courier manual truck that carries a 60 kg parcel up domestic stairs, rolls on flat, locks hands-off on slopes, and stows flat in a small van.
mechanism_sentence: A courier pulls small wheels that walk over each step while a spring brake holds the 60 kg load when the handle is released.
decisive_choices: Keep one-piece twin-tube backbone upsized to 40 by 36 mm over triangulated toe-stay C29 because transverse brace cannot ground cantilever tip per E93 and E115, upsize cuts whip to 43.9 mm per E116 with 40.9 MPa per E118 for 0.37 kg penalty per E117 while stay adds joint in peak 118 N m path per E90 with 503 N tie per E119.

Use tri-star rotating cluster C1 for stair traverse because it is the only working means pivoting over the 197 mm riser with 185 mm radius and 37.3 N m per side costing 129 J per riser, while pull posture C11 does no stepping and fold-down handle note C19 only aids stow.

Use dead-man lever with disc plus tooth park pin C7 with C20 for limiting because release means locked holding 74.6 N m total against 209 N pull and 188 N hold exceeding sustained limits, while friction-only contact brake C3 alone cannot be trusted without positive lock.
open_question: How do lever release feel and tooth-pin engagement behave under full slope load in a hardware bench test?
transfer_line: Load: folding toe-plate -> twin-tube backbone -> tri-star wheel cluster | Measured: dead-man lever -> courier

assumed_constraints.constraint: Parcel centre fixed at 200 mm forward of backrest for all moment and stress checks
Impact factor 1.5 applied to static backbone stress
Tri-star cluster effective radius 185 mm for slope torque

concept.working_principle: Parcel sits on folding toe-plate and straps to twin-tube backbone, paired wheels roll on flat, tri-star clusters pivot over step noses, spring-applied disc plus tooth pin holds slope when lever is released and meters when squeezed, toe folds and handle slides with brace alongside for van stow.

fabrication_steps.description: Weld the twin 1100 mm backbone tubes and axle mounts first, because toe, handle, axle and brace all locate to it
Bolt the folding 365 x 240 mm toe-plate with hinge pin to the backbone root, because it restores the load path when deployed
fabrication_steps.method: Bolted steel plate, 365 x 240 mm with 8 mm pin

fabrication_steps.description: Fit the two tri-star clusters with 150 mm wheels and 160 mm disc plus tooth pin to the main axle, because stair walking and locking are tested together
fabrication_steps.method: Bolted steel clusters with solid rubber wheels, 150 mm wheels, 160 mm rotor

fabrication_steps.description: Run the cable with slack loop from the sliding handle levers to the caliper, then add strap and clip-on brace, because folding must never release the brake
fabrication_steps.method: Cabled steel lever with polyester strap and aluminium brace

risks.risk: Tired hand cannot hold 188 N descent load by grip alone
risks.mitigation: Hold slope in spring-applied disc plus tooth pin with 57.4 N release and hands-off auto-lock, verify by bench test

risks.risk: 110 mm whip mistimes cluster nose contact and 1100 mm backbone cannot enter straight through door
risks.mitigation: Upsize to one-piece 40 by 36 mm tubes for 43.9 mm whip under quarter riser and accept 1150 mm diagonal stow

novelty_claim: Proven tri-star walking with twin-tube backbone plus spring-applied disc with positive tooth lock for hands-off holding and folding toe plus sliding handle for diagonal van stow, beyond fixed-frame 60 kg stair truck with skids.

figure_spec.system_view: Side view of deployed truck with parcel on toe-plate, twin-tube backbone to axle with tri-star clusters on 197 mm step, handle up and brace pinned

open_questions: How do lever release feel and tooth-pin engagement behave under full slope load in a hardware bench test, since calculations show 57.4 N release and 0.498 shear ratio but no hardware test has been run?
